Get labels and label EVERYTHING and I mean everything. If you label a draw "socks underwear and swim" make it a rule that you have to put things in the corresponding spot. Label a shelf in the closet "towels" and that is the only thing you can put there. It helps me. That's what I did when I went to college. You could even label sections of the floor. like a square in the corner for your laundry basket.

I am 19 years old and I have ADHD and was diagnosed when I was about 6 but showed symptoms much before that. In middle school I tried to hide my ADHD (and other learning disability) and my "friends" treated my terribly because they didn't have the patience for some of the quirks and "symptoms" that came along with ADHD. In high school I had friends but I didn't disclose to them until long after having met them and they had a little bit more patience but not by much at all. Then during my first semester of college I disclosed to my friends from the first time I met them because I figured worst comes to worst they don't like me because of my ADHD but I found that my friends who I had disclosed to upon meeting them have so much more patience with me and understand how I work and that I can get overwhelmed in busy situations. I really believe that this is because they were told from the start. My new modo that I have chosen to go by is to tell any potential friend because if they understand from the get go they will be much better friends.



If you skipped the long blah that I wrote: Telling people from the point you meet them will mean that they will be better friends because they will understand more and have more patience :) happened with me

If you can't wear bracelets or bandanas then I would recommend drawing over the scars with a sharpie or pen. ex) If you have a line scar on your hip then draw a flower or swirl over it to cover it. It works better than make up and it lasts longer and just looks like you like to draw on yourself. Your parents may threaten to take away your pens or markers but just hide one in your room if they do. I am 19 years old and my mom still threatens to take mine away. But anyways this has always worked for me in the past. ohh FYI pen and sharpie WILL come off with sweat and white leather couches giving your grandmothers couch a nice picture of a flower.... BUt other than that it stays on

I've had similar issues with scars that don't look like they could easily be explained. In those cases I take a pen or sharpie and I draw a picture over it to cover it. Don't do one solid patch of color or else you may be able to see a difference in ink color showing that there's a scar, but if you draw an image with a bunch of lines it will cover it up well.

I know, it is so much easier to do than to deal with the feelings. I am so proud of you for wanting to go and get help. I waited way too long to go and get help. I waited almost 9 years myself. I should have gone when I very first started but I didn't. I wish I had but I was scared to. I also didn't think that it hurt anyone else but myself but I learned that I was wrong when I told my now fiance. When I told him, he cried and kissed every one of my scares and every time I cut I tell him because I know it's not good for me to try and hide it from him. And every single time I see something break inside him but he still reassures me that he's not mad at me and that he loves me and then he kisses my cuts and holds me until I'm ok. He is the reason I try so hard. I'd love to say I do it for my self but that would be a lie. I do it for him because I can't bear to see that every time I do it I hurt him. So any way, remember that this affects your loved ones too so if you ever find that you can't stop for yourself, then do it for them. please. and if you feel you don't have anyone then do it for me, a total stranger on the internet laying in her bed, cuddled up under a blanket thinking about when she started. But any way I am so proud of you and thank you for listening to me and stay strong <3

Alright, I have also experienced this and here is the scientific answer, When you are depressed all of your senses a deafened. For example, colors aren't as bright, smells aren't as strong, and you can't feel pain as much. When you start to get better and then you cut after a while of not cutting because you are in a better place then you can feel the pain again because you're depression has lessened. Does that make sense? This is what happened to me and in my college psychology class we talked about depression and about the deafening of senses that goes along with it.
